title: No database: data lives in JSON and Markdown files
context: This is a prototype of the triage workflow. Saving changes and letting several people edit are out of scope.
decision: Requests, triage output, requirements and decisions are files in /data, read at build time. Every page is prerendered as static HTML. We revisit this when the UI needs editing.

title: Group requests by meaning with an LLM, and keep the result as a file
context: Clients describe the same need in different words, so grouping by keywords misses most of the overlap.
decision: An LLM grouped the requests into themes and rated pain and effort, using the prompt in data/PROMPT.md. The result is saved in data/triage.json, which is the single source of truth for themes. Raw requests are never edited.

title: Rank by a transparent score, not by request count
context: A loud operator sending many tickets shouldn't outrank a need shared by many operators, and one very large operator shouldn't dominate either.
decision: score = operatorsAsking × pain × log10(totalBookings) ÷ effortWeight (S=1, M=2, L=3). Each operator is counted once per theme. log10 dampens the effect of operator size. Arithmetic is done by code, judgments by the model.

title: Board columns are derived from the ranking
context: A status workflow (New → Done) doesn't say what to build first.
decision: #1 goes to Now, #2–4 go to Next, and the rest plus unclustered requests go to Inbox. Columns are computed from triage.json, not stored.

title: Full requirement docs are Markdown files
context: A requirement doc is long text (quotes, scope, Given/When/Then) that people review and edit as text.
decision: The top theme has a full doc in data/requirements/<themeId>.md, rendered on /requirement/[themeId]. The other themes fall back to the short notes in requirements.json.
